Hi David / Monica,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As part of our internal compliance sign-off we need two things before the 2026-12-20 deadline: a short, operational switchover playbook that describes how traffic will be routed from an EU primary to APAC warm-standby in the event of a regional outage, and formal proof of data residency for the EU primary (logs/audit statements showing data never left the EU cluster for the last 90 days).

Specific asks:
- A one-page switchover checklist for our on-call engineers (DNS TTL changes, BGP peering notes, RBAC access list for the handover).
- Exported audit log samples and a statement of residency for the tenant (time-bounded).
- Any regulatory controls we apply during automatic failover (is there a grace period before cache rehydration to prevent cross-border KV sync?).

If you can attach a draft playbook and any supporting attachments we can circulate to our internal CISO and legal teams.

Best,
Evelyn Park

Evelyn — thanks, understood. Attaching a first draft playbook and a residency Q&A export (redacted ID fields). High level answers inline and attachment stubs below.

Quick summary of our approach:
- EU primary: customer-dedicated VPC deployed in eu-west region with tags locking storage/control plane metadata to the eu project.
- APAC warm-standby: provisioned but passive; no automatic KV replication unless explicitly enabled by the customer. Failover is a manual or semi-automated process initiated by your ops team or by approved Redwood ops runbooks.
- DNS and routing: we rely on a low-ttl CNAME + regional edge rewrite. BGP changes are seldom needed; only in private peering scenarios.

Thanks David — reviewed the draft. Two operational clarifications before we hand this to the customer:

1) KV/cache: by default we do NOT replicate KV across regions. For Euroland's private deploy we keep the KV store local to the EU primary. When customers request warm-standby we do an on-demand snapshot transfer (S3-like encrypted snapshot) to a secure APAC bucket during the maintenance window. That means there is a manual window (15-45 min) for state catch-up after switchover unless they opt into continuous replication (which has a regulatory implication).

2) Routing/data-plane switching: if they use Private Interconnect (direct peering), then we recommend a BGP-preferred failover with pre-configured standby prefixes. If they depend on public DNS, use a low TTL (60s) and regional CDN edge rewrites.

I'm adding a short "authorization checklist" block to the playbook that lists who must sign (CISO, network owner, Redwood ops lead) and what evidence (signed DocuSign + residency log export).

On KV question from Evelyn: "is there a grace period before cache rehydration to prevent cross-border KV sync?" — yes, we keep cache cold until the operator approves rehydration; in the draft playbook that's step 6: operator confirms approval and initiates secure snapshot restore.

Markus
VP, Site Reliability
Redwood Inference
